preserved_objections.basis: Radiative cooling requires clear sky conditions with minimal atmospheric water vapor to function effectively, yet the proposed application targets high humidity environments (90% RH) where atmospheric water vapor blocks the transparency window, making radiative cooling ineffective according to fundamental heat transfer principles

The candidate fails to address the critical boundary condition of water-wick clogging with dissolved salts, which will inevitably occur in real-world use and render both evaporative and radiative cooling mechanisms non-functional within days regardless of coating application

The candidate's evidence includes studies on influenza vaccine reporting guidelines and dairy production statistics, which are completely irrelevant to the thermal management problem being addressed, demonstrating a fundamental disconnect between the proposed solution and available supporting evidence

The radiative cooling coating would need to maintain both high solar reflectivity (>0.95) and strong infrared emissivity (>0.9) while being mechanically durable enough to withstand handling in remote clinic environments, which is technologically impossible with current materials science

The testable prediction fails to specify critical parameters such as coating thickness, application method, or degradation testing protocol, making the measurement impossible to reproduce or validate in real-world conditions
